newsitem.title: USA: Freddie Mac invests in overseas mortgage fund.
newsitem.headline: Freddie Mac invests in overseas mortgage fund.

text.p: U.S. government-sponsored enterprise (GSE) Freddie Mac is investing what insiders have termed a "significant" amount in a $1.0 billion overseas mortgage security fund, market sources said Tuesday.

The FFTW-Freddie Mac Gold PC Mortgage LIBOR Fund Plc., is registered in Ireland. It will be marketed to European institutional investors by Fischer Francis Trees & Watts Inc and Bayerische Vereinsbank A.G..
Fischer Francis Trees will serve as advisor to the fund, which it designed along with Freddie Mac.

Minimum investment in the fund is $1.0 million and it is expected to have a first close on October 1. The fund's benchmark will be six-month London Interbank Offered Rate, and the total amount being raised was $1.0 billion, according to Patricia Cook, managing director at Fischer Francis.

Three-quarters of the fund's investments will be in Freddie Mac Gold PC securities. Freddie Mac buys mortgage loans that meet strict quality criteria from financial institutions that originate home loans. Freddie Mac then uses the loans to create and issue securities.

The remaining 25 percent of the overseas fund's portfolio will be invested in collateralized mortgage obligations and adjustable rate mortgage products as well as mortgage securities guaranteed by the Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA), said Bob Ryan, vice president of Freddie Mac's mortgage securities department. GNMA, a U.S. government agency, buys loans from lenders much like Freddie Mac.

Freddie Mac would not disclose its share in the fund but will participate in the road show marketing the fund. Ryan characterized the government-sponsored enterprise's (GSE) investment in the fund as "significant."
Cook said the fund was "technically a closed-end fund, but there are liquidity provisions. Every six months there is an opportunity to redeem shares."

Ryan said the fund likely would attract financial institutions and corporate treasuries. "The objective of the fund is to achieve spread over LIBOR," said Ryan. Cook added that the fund was geared to any institution "financing themselves on a LIBOR basis."
Ryan said the fund would allow European investors to participate in the U.S. mortgage securities market without having to directly manage the mortgage security portfolios.

Also, the Freddie Mac executive said the fund allowed for a broader investor base in U.S. mortgage securities. "We need to canvas the globe for investors in MBS products. Specifically, we want to increase demand for Gold PCs," said Ryan.

European investors, said Cook, would be attracted to the fund because their "investment alternatives have dwindled from a spread basis. The range of alternatives to meet their targets has been reduced."

The fund's marketing effort, which starts next week, will take Freddie Mac and Fisher Francis officials to investor groups in Munich, Vienna, Geneva, Zurich, Geneva, Paris and Luxembourg as well as Dublin.
Ryan said that the degree of European investor interest in the fund would determine prospects for a similar fund to possibly be developed and marketed in the Pacific Rim.
"If this is successful, we will clearly explore other opportunities. Our next step will be clearly the Pacific Rim," he said.
